title: Appli Ubuntu téléchargement vidéos
desc:
Je cherche à faire développer une application qui tourne nativement sous Ubuntu et me permette de télécharger des vidéos depuis une source que je fournirai.  
L’interface devra être entièrement web : je veux pouvoir lancer le service sur ma machine et accéder à un tableau de bord depuis le navigateur pour piloter les téléchargements.  

Fonctionnalités indispensables :  
• Téléchargement en haute qualité (HD ou équivalent quand disponible).  
• Téléchargement par lot pour pouvoir lancer plusieurs URLs en une seule opération.  
• Choix du format de fichier avant lancement (au minimum MP4 et MP3, avec possibilité d’en ajouter d’autres).  

Exigences techniques et livrables :  
1. Code source propre, commenté, prêt à être cloné et installé sur Ubuntu (22.04 LTS).  
2. Script d’installation ou instructions pas-à-pas pour les dépendances (Python, Node JS ou autre stack libre, au choix).  
3. Interface web réactive : liste des tâches, état de progression, logs d’erreurs, possibilité de pause/reprise et annulation.  
4. Gestion des erreurs réseau et reprise automatique quand c’est possible.  
5. Fichier README détaillant la configuration, l’usage et la façon d’ajouter de nouveaux formats de sortie.  

Je suis ouvert aux librairies courantes (youtube-dl, yt-dlp, ffmpeg, etc.) tant que la licence reste compatible et que l’intégration est propre. Indiquez votre stack proposée, le délai estimé et un aperçu de votre approche pour la conversion de formats et la gestion des lots.

title: Host Legacy VB App Online
desc:
The Visual Basic program I currently run straight from a USB stick needs to move to the cloud without changing how it behaves. My goal is simple: open the same interface and get the same results, only now over the internet instead of from a pen drive.

Preferred environment is a Linux server. I’m open to whichever method makes most sense there—Wine, a lightweight Windows VM, containerisation, or even a web-friendly wrapper—as long as the end-user experience stays identical.

Database handling is the one grey area: the app might be using flat files or an old Access database. I’ll need advice on whether we keep that structure, migrate to MySQL/MariaDB, or adopt another engine that plays nicely under Linux.

What I’d like from you:
• A proposed approach that preserves all current functionality.  
• Milestones with realistic timelines for assessment, migration, testing and go-live.  
• Any licensing or third-party costs I should plan for.  
• Your total price (or a clear pricing model) so I can sign off quickly.

Final deliverable is a fully-hosted version I can reach remotely via standard browser or lightweight client, plus concise deployment and maintenance notes so I can replicate the set-up later.

Let me know what project files or screenshots you need from me to give a precise quote.

title: Animal Transcription Start Codon Identification
desc:
I am compiling a concise reference on the start codons that initiate transcription in animals and need a specialist who can gather, verify, and clearly present this information. The scope is confined to the animal kingdom; bacteria, plants, and other taxa are out of scope for this task.   

Here is what I need from you:  
• A brief explanation of what qualifies as a transcriptional start codon in animals, backed by up-to-date primary literature.  
• A definitive list of every recognized start codon, noting any species-specific or lineage-specific variants if they exist.  
• Supporting evidence for each codon: journal citations, GenBank or Ensembl accession numbers, or other reputable database links.  
• A short commentary (a few sentences each) on any controversies, recently discovered alternatives, or unresolved questions in the field.  

Please deliver your findings as a well-structured Word or Google Docs report plus a separate spreadsheet (CSV or Excel) containing the codon sequence, associated species (where relevant), evidence link, and citation. I will review for completeness, correct citations, and clarity before release.   

A background in molecular genetics or bioinformatics—and the ability to navigate databases such as NCBI, Ensembl, or UCSC Genome Browser—will make this straightforward for you.

title: MikroTik ISP Router Configuration
desc:
I have a MikroTik running RouterOS that I want to turn into a mini-ISP edge. The box will sit behind several uplinks—one of them is a Starlink terminal and I may add fibre, DSL or cable later—so the configuration must bond or load-balance multiple connections and fail over cleanly.

Downstream, each customer plugs in their own router and receives an address via my DHCP pool. I need to be able to set a per-Mbps cap for every client, enforce a sensible firewall policy, and keep management, customer traffic and any future VoIP on separate VLANs.

Key elements I expect from you:
• Multi-WAN bonding / load balancing that includes Starlink  
• Fully functional DHCP server handing out the ranges I specify  
• Bandwidth control per user (simple queues or queue trees—your call)  
• Robust firewall rules for basic security and DDoS protection  
• VLAN scheme that isolates management and customer networks  

Deliverables
1. An import-ready .rsc (or step-by-step CLI script) covering the entire configuration  
2. A concise guide explaining how to add or remove uplinks, create new speed profiles, and expand VLANs  
3. A live remote session to load the config, test throughput, verify fail-over and confirm firewall rule hits  

Please rely only on standard RouterOS features (WinBox or pure CLI is fine). Once your setup lets me plug in a customer router, assign their speed, and watch traffic switch seamlessly between bonded links when one line drops, the job is complete.
